note: All results company-reported, no independent replication. Drawn counts schematic. Three headline numbers.

numbers.2,500: Opening, print p2, May daily merged changes company-reported average.
numbers.30,000: Opening, print p2, September daily merged changes company-reported lower bound.
numbers.200: Scaling Scion, print p8; CPU and memory infrastructure footprint vs prior Git mirrors; not speed, total CI, or dollars.

claims.l01: Opening and Growing our monorepo: agents and online jobs made source control the development bottleneck.
claims.l02: Opening, print p2: May average around 2,500 merged changes/day; September over 30,000/day.
claims.l03: Growing our monorepo: used Git mirror fleet; operational load grew.
claims.l04: Growing our monorepo: Git shallow/sparse/promisor features already used; limits apply to Anthropic's workload.
claims.l05: Principles: always-online clients, designed around reachable server.
claims.l06: Principles and Scaling Scion: client requests only needed trees/blobs. Warehouse schematic is a namespace, no full repo on any server.
claims.l07: Scaling Scion: requests specific immutable trees and blobs.
claims.l08: Scaling Scion: any cache can answer an immutable request; node daemon shares stored objects.
claims.l09: Scaling Scion: daemon talks to regional scion-cache for missing objects.
claims.l10: Scaling Scion: cache misses ask authoritative servers, which read Spanner or cloud storage as needed.
claims.l11: Scaling Scion: objects stream through cache tiers and jobs on node reuse same objects.
claims.l12: Principles: server computes history, merges, commits; API jobs can avoid checkout.
claims.l13: Scaling Scion, print p8: Anthropic reports infrastructure CPU and memory requirements 200x smaller than prior Git mirroring infrastructure.
claims.l14: Same measurement: comparison only source-control infrastructure vs prior Git mirrors.
claims.l15: Conclusion: unusual enormous-monorepo workload; expressly unsuitable general Git replacement.
claims.l16: Teaching inference from case study, qualified by may; no measured future outcome.
